rules_overview_title: The Rules of Men's Rhythmic Gymnastics
rules_overview_lead: What to know first if you are watching or competing for the first time. Written in our own words, based on the official rule book.
rules_overview_caution: This page covers only the essentials. Official decisions rest on the rule books of the governing bodies.
rules_overview_group_summary: Five gymnasts perform together, without apparatus
rules_overview_group_body: Judges look at whether the five move as one and whether the routine holds together. A team of four may compete, but is deducted for it. If even one gymnast drops out mid-routine, the routine stops there.
rules_overview_individual_summary: One gymnast performs with one apparatus
rules_overview_individual_body: Each apparatus has its own character, so the same gymnast looks different from event to event. Some competitions rank the total of all four events, others rank each event separately.
rules_overview_apparatus_heading: Four apparatus in the individual event
rules_overview_apparatus_stick_body: Two sticks. They are spun separately in each hand, thrown and swapped. The thing to watch is whether both turn at the same speed, together.
rules_overview_apparatus_ring_body: A hoop. It is passed around the body, rolled, thrown and jumped through. Because it is large, the height of a throw and the place it is caught are easy to follow.
rules_overview_apparatus_rope_body: A rope. Jumped through, swung and knotted. It holds no shape of its own, so the handling within the hands is fine and detailed.
rules_overview_apparatus_clubs_body: Two clubs. Much of the work is continuous small rotation, and the difference shows in whether body skills can be added while the clubs keep turning.
rules_overview_floor_body: The floor is a 13 m by 13 m square. Stepping — or letting the apparatus go — outside the line is deducted. A safety zone is kept around it.
rules_overview_time_body: A timing judge measures the routine. Both shorter and longer than the set length are deducted, so routines are built to the second.
rules_overview_score_heading: Three sets of eyes make the score
rules_overview_score_lead: One routine is watched by separate judges from separate angles.
rules_overview_score_d_body: The value of what was performed. Two judges confirm the skills and agree on a shared value score.
rules_overview_score_a_body: Composition, the relationship with the music, and the variety of skills. Four judges score out of 10.
rules_overview_score_e_body: How well it was done. Broken posture, a dropped apparatus and the like are taken off. Four judges score out of 10.
rules_overview_score_note: For A and E, the highest and lowest of the four are dropped and the rest averaged. One extreme score moves the result very little.
rules_overview_deduction_body: Going out of bounds, being over or under time, and competing short-handed are taken off the final score by the head judge, separately from the scoring of the routine itself.
rules_overview_music_body: Every routine is performed to music. Instruments or the human voice are both allowed, and lyrics are permitted as long as the content is appropriate. That is why the range of music is wide.
rules_overview_costume_body: A close-fitting top and trousers. No skin is shown other than the head, face, neck, hands and arms. The top is not worn outside the trousers. In the group event, all five match in cut and colour.
rules_overview_costume_note: A common misunderstanding: the sleeveless leotard belongs to women's rhythmic gymnastics. Men compete in long sleeves and long trousers.
rules_overview_full_text_body: A page carrying the articles themselves is ready, but it stays closed while we confirm that we may publish them. Once that is settled, it will be added below this page.
rules_overview_link_judge_body: Score a routine yourself, and you start to see it as a judge does.
rules_overview_link_music_body: How the music for a routine is put together, and how to choose it.
rules_overview_link_calendar_body: When and where the next competition is. Find one you can go and watch.
